title: Boss: the rule engine
summary: Turn written rules into exact, readable conditions.

steps.title: Module boss
body: Real rules arrive as English sentences. Your job is to turn each one into a condition that is exactly right at the edges. Before writing code, list one input that should pass and one that should fail for each part of the rule.

steps.title: Exclusive or
prompt: Write `bool Xor(bool a, bool b)` that is `true` when **exactly one** of `a` and `b` is true, using only `&&`, `||` and `!` (no `^`, no `!=`).
hints: "Exactly one" is "at least one" AND "not both".

steps.title: Strong password
prompt: Write `string Check(string pw)` with guard clauses. Return the **first** problem found, in this order:
`char.IsDigit(c)` and `char.IsUpper(c)` test a single character; `pw.Any(char.IsDigit)` tests the whole string.
template: Dojo.Eq("Check(\"short\") reports length first", "too short", Check("short"));
hints: One `if ... return` per rule, in the order given.

steps.title: Overlapping bookings
prompt: Two bookings run from `start1` to `end1` and from `start2` to `end2` (hours, end not included: a booking from 9 to 10 and one from 10 to 11 do **not** overlap).
Write `bool Overlaps(int start1, int end1, int start2, int end2)`.
Tip: it is easier to say when they do **not** overlap (one ends before the other starts), then negate that with De Morgan.
solution: bool Overlaps(int start1, int end1, int start2, int end2)
template: Dojo.Eq("9-10 and 10-11 do not overlap", false, Overlaps(9, 10, 10, 11));
Dojo.Eq("13-14 and 9-10 do not overlap", false, Overlaps(13, 14, 9, 10));
hints: They do not overlap when `end1 <= start2 || end2 <= start1`.

steps.title: What is behind each door?
prompt: Every floor of Delve has dead ends, numbered 1, 2, 3, ... (the numbers keep counting up from floor to floor). **`static char Encounter(int room)`** decides what waits in room `room`, as the map tile:
- a multiple of **3 and 5**: `'m'`, a mimic (a chest with teeth)

The rules are listed in priority order: room 21 is a multiple of 3 **and** of 7, and it holds a goblin. Room 35 (5 and 7) holds a chest. Work out rooms 15, 21, 35, 49 and 105 by hand before you run anything; the order of your checks decides them.

forbid.message: Every function starts with `static` (Delve keeps its pieces in one static class)

hints: This is FizzBuzz with a fourth answer. Which check has to come first so that 15 is not caught by the "3" rule?
Checking `room % 15 == 0` first covers "3 and 5". The 7 rule goes last of the four, because 3 and 5 both beat it.

build.title: Encounters
build.unlocks: Delve's dead ends fill with goblins, chests, mimics and potions.
